investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable capacity, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 132–154 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never started, no vmId was assigned, and remoteState never reached running/idle/ready. This is a runtime infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; this call depends on a schedulable pod — if the pod is rejected the runner cannot proceed to collect any evidence.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling messages.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only 2 nodes (those with kata.peerpods.io/vm), and those 2 nodes are at capacity. If the selector was recently narrowed or node labels changed, previously schedulable nodes may now be excluded.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 2 nodes capable of running kata peer-pod workloads. If concurrent remote agent creation requests (e.g., from other users or parallel eval runs) consumed all slots before this probe ran, the probe would see the same exhaustion message.

QUATERNARY — Preemption disabled or ineffective: the scheduler message explicitly states 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling', meaning no lower-priority pods exist on the 2 eligible nodes that could be evicted to make room.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and returns vmIdPresent=true with a valid remoteState, the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a competing workload released its VM slot) rather than a persistent capacity ceiling.

If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero and no pods are consuming it, the root cause is not resource exhaustion but rather a misconfigured resource request in the pod spec (e.g., requesting more VM units than exist).

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured such that it excludes all 6 nodes (not just 4), the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message would be a secondary symptom and the affinity misconfiguration would be the primary cause.

If the 2 nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity are found to be in a NotReady or cordoned state, the scheduler message would be misleading and the real cause would be node unavailability rather than resource exhaustion.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources at the time of the failure, the extended resource may have been removed or misconfigured on the nodes, making the reported capacity of 0 a node registration issue rather than a workload saturation issue.

Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote agent pods remain after each probe cycle, catching cases where withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs fails to release VM slots.
Add a node-affinity smoke eval that verifies at least one schedulable node matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector has non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before the creation probe runs.

investigation.title: Remote Agents eval failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion blocks all remote agent pod scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every probe pod was stuck unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the state-polling step, so zero required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the two eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) is identical across all three sibling checks, confirming the failure is at the VM-slot layer before any agent API call is made. The eval runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905 calls createAgent with type "remote", which triggers pod creation; that pod never became schedulable within the 154 s the eval waited, so no evidence was written and the contract gap covers all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage — no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary — the four remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules (e.g., a label or taint mismatch), meaning even if VM slots were freed on those nodes they could not accept the pod. This is a contributing constraint that narrows the schedulable node pool to two.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining allocatable capacity, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Because the pod remained unscheduled for 132–154 seconds across all three checks, the agent VM was never started, no vmId was assigned, and remoteState never reached running/idle/ready. This is a runtime infrastructure capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; the impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling messages.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod's affinity rules target only 2 nodes (those with kata.peerpods.io/vm), and those 2 nodes are at capacity. If the selector was recently narrowed or node labels changed, previously schedulable nodes may now be excluded.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the production cluster has only 2 nodes capable of running kata peer-pod workloads. If concurrent remote agent creation requests (e.g., from other users or parallel eval runs) consumed all slots before this probe ran, the probe would see the same exhaustion message.

QUATERNARY — Preemption disabled or ineffective: the scheduler message explicitly states 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod' and 'Preemption is not helpful for scheduling', meaning no lower-priority pods exist on the 2 eligible nodes that could be evicted to make room.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe never reached the agent runtime, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero viable nodes and no preemption candidates available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~132–154 s across all three checks), preventing the eval runner from creating an agent, reaching its runtime, or collecting any response evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or real workloads have consumed all allocatable VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node selector, meaning the effective schedulable pool is already constrained to only 2 nodes, amplifying any capacity pressure.

Tertiary — prior eval run cleanup failure: if the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1916) did not successfully delete agent pods from a previous run, those pods may still be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots, starving new probe attempts.

Quaternary — cluster-level VM quota reduction: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes may have been reduced (e.g., node resize, resource limit change) without a corresponding reduction in concurrent probe load.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted (i.e., allocatable slots are available and unused), the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the node affinity/selector mismatch would become the primary suspect.

If no stuck or leaked remote-agent pods are found holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, the cleanup hypothesis is disproved and the cause is more likely a quota reduction or a surge in legitimate workload.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but are excluded only by node affinity, and that affinity is intentional and correct, then the failure is purely a capacity problem on the 2 eligible nodes rather than a misconfiguration.
If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds without any infrastructure change, it would suggest a transient capacity spike rather than a persistent exhaustion condition.

If the local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) are also failing with scheduling errors, the problem may be broader than the remote kata VM pool; if they are passing, the failure is confirmed to be isolated to the remote kata.peerpods.io/vm resource.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all nodes before attempting remote-agent probe creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check rather than a timeout.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent probe pods remain running after each observability workflow execution, catching slot leakage before it affects the next run.

Add an eval that tracks the count of schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm slots over time and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), providing early warning before full exhaustion.
Consider a dedicated eval for node affinity/selector health that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's selector, alerting if the eligible pool shrinks below a minimum.
